learningObjective: See the backdoor path that makes an observed support-message association differ from the intervention effect.
mediumRationale: The lesson is topological rather than quantitative. A compact causal DAG makes the competing paths visible and remains editable with the article.

deckReview.notes: The 214-slide source deck was searched by extracted headings and text. It does not contain a dedicated causal-inference or confounding slide, so the visual is derived from this article's worked example rather than imitating a deck figure.

sources.title: Causal Inference: What If
sources.usage: Used to check the treatment, outcome, confounding, and adjustment terminology. The diagram is an original redraw for the article's support-message example.
sources.license: No source figure copied; conceptual reference only.

sourceReview.notes: The article-specific three-node DAG is sufficient. A paper figure would add complexity without improving the core mental model.

agentReview.summary: Recommended Mermaid for a compact treatment-confounder-outcome DAG, with the causal edge emphasized and the two confounding edges distinguished by line style.

implementation.accessibility: The Mermaid source includes an accessible title and full description. Labels and line styles preserve the lesson without relying on color, and a prose caption repeats the inference.
